# apple_subscription_offer_code (Resource)

Manages a subscription offer code: a discount or free period on one auto-renewable subscription, redeemed with a code. It is the App Store's nearest thing to a coupon, and like a coupon it targets one plan — one subscription, so one tier and one billing period.

The offer carries no codes itself. Customers redeem it through an `apple_subscription_offer_code_custom_code` (one shared string, such as `SCHOOL2026`) or an `apple_subscription_offer_code_one_time_use_code` (a batch of single-use codes Apple generates).

~> **Every attribute but `active` is fixed at creation.** Apple's update request carries `active` alone, so any other change — the name, who is eligible, the duration, a price — replaces the offer: a new one is created and the old one is deactivated, **invalidating every code already handed out for it**. Treat a running offer as immutable; to change the terms of a campaign, add a new offer beside it.

~> **Nothing here can be deleted.** App Store Connect API 4.5.1 publishes no `DELETE` for an offer code, a custom code or a batch of one-time-use codes. `terraform destroy` **deactivates** the record (`active = false`), warns, and drops it from state; the record and its codes stay in App Store Connect forever. App Store Connect's help says a deactivated offer "can't be reactivated later" and that every code under it is invalidated, so deactivating — by destroy, by a replacement, or by setting `active = false` — is final for the codes customers already hold.

App Store Connect allows at most 10 active offers per subscription at a time.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_apps" "example" {
  bundle_id = "com.example.app"
}

resource "apple_subscription_group" "premium" {
  app_id         = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
  reference_name = "Premium"
}

resource "apple_subscription" "pro_annual" {
  group_id            = apple_subscription_group.premium.id
  product_id          = "com.example.app.pro.annual"
  name                = "Pro Annual"
  subscription_period = "ONE_YEAR"
}

# An offer code targets one subscription -- one tier, one billing period --
# the way a coupon restricted to one price does.
#
# A free trial has no price, only the territories it is offered in.
resource "apple_subscription_offer_code" "schools_free_month" {
  subscription_id        = apple_subscription.pro_annual.id
  name                   = "Schools free month 2026"
  customer_eligibilities = ["NEW", "EXPIRED"]
  offer_eligibility      = "STACK_WITH_INTRO_OFFERS"
  duration               = "ONE_MONTH"
  offer_mode             = "FREE_TRIAL"
  number_of_periods      = 1

  prices = [
    { territory_id = "AUS" },
    { territory_id = "USA" },
  ]
}

# A paid offer names one of the subscription's own price points per
# territory: 49.99 in the USA for the first year, and whatever Apple
# considers equivalent elsewhere.
data "apple_subscription_price_points" "discount_usa" {
  subscription_id = apple_subscription.pro_annual.id
  territories     = ["USA"]
  customer_price  = "49.99"
}

data "apple_subscription_price_point_equalizations" "discount" {
  price_point_id = data.apple_subscription_price_points.discount_usa.price_points[0].id
  territories    = ["AUS", "GBR"]
}

resource "apple_subscription_offer_code" "half_price_first_year" {
  subscription_id        = apple_subscription.pro_annual.id
  name                   = "Half price first year"
  customer_eligibilities = ["NEW"]
  offer_eligibility      = "REPLACE_INTRO_OFFERS"
  duration               = "ONE_YEAR"
  offer_mode             = "PAY_UP_FRONT"
  number_of_periods      = 1

  prices = [
    for territory, price_point in merge(
      { USA = data.apple_subscription_price_points.discount_usa.price_points[0].id },
      data.apple_subscription_price_point_equalizations.discount.price_point_ids,
      ) : {
      territory_id   = territory
      price_point_id = price_point
    }
  ]

  # Every attribute but active is fixed at creation, and a replacement
  # deactivates the old offer -- invalidating codes already handed out. If
  # Apple revises its equalizations, keep the running offer rather than
  # replacing it.
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [prices]
  }
}

# Ending a campaign: active = false deactivates the offer in place, for good.
# Apple cannot reactivate it; setting it back to true plans a new offer.
resource "apple_subscription_offer_code" "spring_2026" {
  subscription_id        = apple_subscription.pro_annual.id
  name                   = "Spring 2026"
  customer_eligibilities = ["EXPIRED"]
  offer_eligibility      = "STACK_WITH_INTRO_OFFERS"
  duration               = "ONE_WEEK"
  offer_mode             = "FREE_TRIAL"
  number_of_periods      = 2
  prices                 = [{ territory_id = "USA" }]
  active                 = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `customer_eligibilities` (Set of String) Who may redeem the offer: any of `NEW` (never subscribed), `EXISTING` (currently subscribed) and `EXPIRED` (subscribed before and lapsed). Cannot be changed after creation.
- `duration` (String) The length of one offer period: `THREE_DAYS`, `ONE_WEEK`, `TWO_WEEKS`, `ONE_MONTH`, `TWO_MONTHS`, `THREE_MONTHS`, `SIX_MONTHS` or `ONE_YEAR`. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `name` (String) The offer's reference name in App Store Connect. Customers do not see it. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `number_of_periods` (Number) How many `duration` periods the offer lasts. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `offer_eligibility` (String) How the offer combines with the subscription's introductory offer: `STACK_WITH_INTRO_OFFERS` or `REPLACE_INTRO_OFFERS`. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `offer_mode` (String) How the customer pays during the offer: `PAY_AS_YOU_GO` (a discounted price each period), `PAY_UP_FRONT` (one discounted price for the whole offer) or `FREE_TRIAL` (nothing). Cannot be changed after creation.
- `prices` (Attributes Set) The offer's price in each territory it is offered in, one element per territory. Required by Apple's create request. A set, because the order carries no meaning. Cannot be changed after creation — Apple publishes no way to add, change or remove an offer's price — so a change replaces the offer.

A price is never a number: `price_point_id` is one of Apple's price points for **this subscription**, read through `apple_subscription_price_points` or `apple_subscription_price_point_equalizations`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--prices))
- `subscription_id` (String) The ID of the `apple_subscription` the offer discounts. Cannot be changed after creation.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether customers can redeem the offer. Defaults to `true`. Setting it to `false` ends the campaign **in place** and keeps the record in the configuration — and is **final**: App Store Connect cannot reactivate an offer, and every code under it is invalidated. Setting it back to `true` therefore plans a **new** offer rather than an update.
- `auto_renew_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the subscription renews automatically once the offer ends. Optional; Apple decides when it is unset, and reports its answer. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `target_subscription_plan_type` (String) Which plan of the subscription the offer applies to: `MONTHLY` (the recurring price) or `UPFRONT` (a pre-paid plan). Optional; Apple decides when it is unset. Cannot be changed after creation.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique Apple-generated identifier for the offer code.
- `production_code_count` (Number) How many of those codes redeem in production.
- `sandbox_code_count` (Number) How many of those codes redeem in the sandbox.
- `total_number_of_codes` (Number) How many codes Apple reports for the offer across both environments.

<a id="nestedatt--prices"></a>
### Nested Schema for `prices`

Required:

- `territory_id` (String) The three-letter Apple territory code, for example `USA`, `GBR` or `AUS`.

Optional:

- `price_point_id` (String) The ID of the Apple price point the customer pays during the offer in this territory. Required for `PAY_AS_YOU_GO` and `PAY_UP_FRONT`; omit it for a `FREE_TRIAL`, which has no price — Apple's schema makes it optional for that reason.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# The import ID is Apple's offer code ID. The subscription is read back with
# it, and so are the prices. apple_subscription_offer_codes lists a
# subscription's offers, including ones made by hand in App Store Connect.
terraform import apple_subscription_offer_code.schools_free_month 6748301234
```
